kind-version: the reasons given for 'our maths is the kind version' do not apply to Rohan's case, which the outro defines as no new spending and he is never late. Losing the grace period only affects new purchases, and late fees only come with a late payment. So 'Late fees come on top' is wrong for an on-time payer and the framing misleads. Fix: say 'And our maths is the kind version. Real cards work out interest every day, on the balance before your payment lands. And keep using the card, and new purchases start charging interest from day one.' Keep event g on word 'day' (first) or retarget it to 'every', event f on word 'purchases'. Box lines: 'Interest charged daily' (at g) and 'New buys: interest from day one' (at f). Change the f sfx from fail to pop or keep it at low gain.

outro (minor, fix while rewriting): the end card CTA 'Find the three year line on your statement' is aimed at a global audience, but only US statements carry it (Reg Z 1026.7(b)(12)). Change it to 'On a US card? Find the three year line'.
